title: Why Do Onions Make You Cry?
description:
Why Do Onions Make You Cry?
A Pip and Ray science short. Educational, not medical advice.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: Ow! My EYES! I barely touched this onion... and I'm CRYING?!

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: You're not sad. The onion... sprayed you.

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: Cutting an onion breaks its cells... and that starts a tiny chemical factory. Watch...

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: Inside the onion, sulfur compounds wait quietly. But when the knife breaks the cells, two enzymes jump out... and build a brand-new GAS!

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: That gas floats up... right into your eyes.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: A gas? Why would my eyes care about a GAS?!

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: The gas lands on the wet surface of your eyes... and STINGS! Tiny nerves in your eyes sound the alarm: something's attacking!

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: So your tear glands FLOOD your eyes... to wash the irritant away.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: So my tears are just... my eyes doing the dishes?!

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: Ha! Pretty much! And a cold onion lets less of that gas escape... so chill it first, and fewer tears!

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: Next time... the onion goes in the FRIDGE!
